rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿĀd lived in a fertile region that God made barren after their punishment; their territory lay from Oman through Hadramawt to Yemen, and they worshipped idols.
rows.anchor: أخصب بلاد فسخط الله عليهم فجعلها مفاوز وكانت بنواحي عمان إلى حضرموت إلى اليمن وكانوا يعبدون الأصنام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After ʿĀd perished, Hūd and the believers went to Mecca and remained there until they died.
rows.anchor: ولما هلكوا لحق هود ومن آمن معه بمكة فلم يزالوا بها حتى ماتوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The faʾ introducing Hūd's speech answers an implied question: what did he say to them? He said, O my people.
rows.anchor: فقال بالفاء لأنه جواب سؤال مقدر أي فما قال لهم يا قوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hūd's question is a gentle appeal and an urging to attain piety.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله أفلا تتقون استعطاف وتحضيض على تحصيل التقوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because Noah's flood was an unparalleled, widely known event and Hūd's generation remembered it, Hūd could warn by asking whether they would not fear.
rows.anchor: فقوله أفلا تتقون إشارة إلى التخويف بتلك الواقعة المشهورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The added description that Hūd's chiefs disbelieved may distinguish them because Murthad ibn Saʿd ibn ʿUfayr believed, unlike Noah's chiefs; alternatively, it may simply condemn them.
rows.anchor: ولم يكن في أشراف قوم نوح مؤمن ألا ترى إلى قولهم وما نراك اتبعك إلا الذين هم أراذلنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb لنراك may describe seeing with the eyes or seeing with the heart, as in the discussion of Noah's story.
rows.anchor: ولنراك يحتمل أن يكون من رؤية العين ومن رؤية القلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: سفاهة means lightness of forbearance and unsoundness of intellect; the construction في سفاهة portrays Hūd as contained within folly.
rows.anchor: وفي سفاهة أي في خفة حلم وسخافة عقل حيث تترك دين قومك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah spoke more forcefully by warning of a great punishment and was answered more harshly; Hūd's gentler appeal drew the milder charge of folly.
rows.anchor: ولما كان كلام نوح لقومه أشد من كلام هود تقوية لقوله إني أخاف عليكم عذاب يوم عظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their charge that Hūd lied suggests he had warned them of punishment if they did not fear God, or it may target his claim that they had no god but God because they claimed other gods.
rows.anchor: فدل ذلك على أنه أخبرهم بما يحل بهم من العذاب إن لم يتقوا الله أو علقوا الظن بقوله ما لكم من إله غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exegetes take ظن either as certainty or as preferring one of two possible alternatives; al-Ḥasan and al-Zajjāj hold the latter reading.
rows.anchor: الظن هنا بمعنى اليقين أو بمعنى ترجيح أحد الجائزين قولان للمفسرين والثاني للحسن والزجاج

rows.speaker: الكرماني
rows.claim: Al-Kirmānī says Noah's people called him misguided because he labored to build a huge ship in a dry wilderness where there was no water.
rows.anchor: وقال الكرماني: خوف نوح الكفار بالطوفان العام واشتغل بعمل السفينة فقالوا إنا لنراك في ضلال مبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hūd's denial echoes his earlier denial in Noah's story; the nominal sentence أنا لكم ناصح أمين matches the nominal sentence in his opponents' last reply.
rows.anchor: تقدمت كيفية هذا النفي في قوله ليس بي ضلالة وهناك جاء وأنصح لكم وهنا جاء وأنا لكم ناصح أمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Trustworthiness is a supreme quality, and the trust of delivering revelation to accountable people is the greatest trust; Hūd was known as sincere and reliable.
rows.anchor: وبالأمانة فيما أقول فلا ينبغي أن أكذب

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says أمين may mean trusted with revelation and the reminder sent by God, or trusted concerning the people, their secrets, and willing their good, or a source of security from deceit and falsehood.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وقوله أمين يحتمل أن يريد على الوحي والذكر النازل من قبل الله

rows.speaker: القشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayrī contrasts God defending Muhammad from delusion and madness with Noah and Hūd defending themselves by denying folly.
rows.anchor: قال القشيري: شتان ما بين من دفع عنه ربه بقوله ما ضل صاحبكم وما غوى

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī praises the prophets' calm, forgiving replies to accusations; God recounts them to teach servants how to address fools and overlook their insults.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: وفي إجابة الأنبياء عليهم السلام من نسبهم إلى الضلالة والسفاهة بما أجابوهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hūd gives warning as the single reason for sending a reminder, omitting the further results of warning: piety and hope for mercy.
rows.anchor: أتى هنا بعلة واحدة وهي الإنذار وهو التخويف بالعذاب واختصر ما يترتب على الإنذار

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī and Ibn Isḥāq explain خلفاء من بعد قوم نوح as people inhabiting the earth after Noah's people.
rows.anchor: سكان الأرض بعدهم قاله السدي وابن إسحاق

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī reads خلفاء as kings whom God installed on earth.
rows.anchor: أو جعلكم ملوكا في الأرض استخلفكم فيها قاله الزمخشري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reminder that they came after Noah indicates that Hūd's people were close in time to Noah's generation.
rows.anchor: وتذكير هود بذلك يدل على قرب زمانهم من زمان نوح لقوله من بعد قوم نوح

rows.speaker: الحوفي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥawfī treats إذ as a time adverb, with the object of اذكروا omitted and understood as God's favors at that time; the verb governing إذ is implicit in the blessing.
rows.anchor: وإذ ظرف في قول الحوفي فيكون مفعول اذكروا محذوفا أي واذكروا آلاء الله عليكم

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī instead parses إذ as the direct object of اذكروا: remember the time God made you successors.
rows.anchor: وفي قول الزمخشري إذ مفعول به وهو منصوب باذكروا أي اذكروا وقت جعلكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بسطة can mean extension, height, and beauty of form; الخلق may mean created people or the act of creation.
rows.anchor: ظاهر التواريخ أن البسطة الامتداد والطول والجمال في الصور والأشكال فيحتمل إذ ذاك أن يكون الخلق بمعنى المخلوقين ويحتمل أن يكون مصدرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means God increased their stature with length and handsome form; reports give their heights as 60 to 100 cubits, 70, 80, or 12 cubits according to different authorities.
rows.anchor: أي وزادكم في خلقكم بسطة أي مد وطول وحسن خلقكم قيل: كان أقصرهم ستين ذراعا وأطولهم مائة ذراع

rows.speaker: الكلبي والسدي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī and al-Suddī say the shortest of ʿĀd was 60 cubits and the tallest 100.
rows.anchor: قاله الكلبي والسدي

rows.speaker: أبو حمزة اليماني
rows.claim: Abū Ḥamza al-Yamānī gives their height as 70 cubits.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حمزة اليماني: سبعون ذراعا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās gives their height as 80 cubits.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس ثمانون ذراعا

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil gives their height as 12 cubits.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: اثنا عشر ذراعا

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Wahb describes their heads as huge as domes, with eyes and nostrils large enough for hyenas to hatch or enter.
rows.anchor: وقال وهب: كان رأس أحدهم مثل القبة العظيمة وعينه تفرخ فيها الضباع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If الخلق means created people, it may refer to Noah's people, their contemporaries, or all people.
rows.anchor: فالخلق قوم نوح أو أهل زمانهم أو الناس كلهم أقوال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations make their increase physical reach, or strength and endurance rather than size, or shared tribal solidarity and mutual support, or power and dominion over others.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الزيادة في الإجرام وهي ما تصل إليه يد الإنسان إذا رفعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hūd first recalls specific blessings—succession and bodily stature—then all God's favors generally; remembering them should lead to exclusive worship, while another interpretation takes اذكروا as give thanks.
rows.anchor: ذكرهم أولا بإنعامه عليهم حيث جعلهم خلفاء وزادهم بسطة وذكرهم ثانيا بنعمه عليهم مطلقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idolaters may acknowledge God but resist abandoning inherited idols, or they may deny God and mean that they would worship God only according to Hūd's claim; Ibn ʿAṭiyya prefers the first for them and idolaters generally.
rows.anchor: الظاهر أنهم أنكروا أن يتركوا أصنامهم ويفردوا الله بالعبادة مع اعترافهم بالله

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the first reading is more evident for these people and idolaters; only those claiming divinity for themselves, such as Pharaoh and Nimrod, deny God's lordship.
rows.anchor: وقال التأويل الأول أظهر فيهم وفي عباد الأوثان ولا يجحد ربوبية الله من الكفرة إلا من ادعاها لنفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone deserves worship because He alone bestows blessings, while idols are inert and powerless; when Hūd's proof left no answer, his people fell back on blind imitation.
rows.anchor: وكان في قول هود لقومه فاذكروا آلاء الله دليل قاطع على أنه لا يعبد إلا المنعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their question about Hūd's coming may mean literal arrival after being apart from them, or sarcastically imply that they thought God sent only angels and Hūd had come from heaven.
rows.anchor: والمجيء هنا يحتمل أن يكون حقيقة بكونه متغيبا عن قومه منفردا بعبادة ربه ثم أرسله الله إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another figurative reading takes جاء as turned toward them or addressed them with the burden of worship, rather than literal travel.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون قولهم ذلك على سبيل الاستهزاء لأنهم كانوا يعتقدون أن الله لا يرسل إلا الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the figurative reading, their question means that Hūd turned to them to impose exclusive worship and its obligations.
rows.anchor: كأنهم قالوا أقصدتنا لنعبد الله وحده وتعرضت لنا بتكاليف ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their demand to bring the promised punishment shows Hūd had warned them of punishment if they persisted in disbelief; they were committed to denying him and contemptuous of prophecy.
rows.anchor: وفي قولهم فأتنا بما تعدنا دليل على أنه كان يعدهم بعذاب الله إن داموا على الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their conditional challenge may test whether Hūd is truthful about his prophethood or about the punishment's arrival.
rows.anchor: أي في نبوتك وإرسالك أو في أن العذاب نازل بنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: رجس وغضب means punishment has come upon them and is now certain.
rows.anchor: قال قد وقع عليكم من ربكم رجس وغضب أي حل بكم وتحتم عليكم

rows.speaker: زيد بن أسلم والأكثرون
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam and most exegetes take رجس as punishment, deriving it from a word for violent shaking.
rows.anchor: قال زيد بن أسلم والأكثرون: الرجس هنا العذاب من الارتجاس وهو الاضطراب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets رجس as divine displeasure.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: السخط

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Rāzī rejects punishment as the meaning because the punishment had not yet occurred at that moment.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبد الله الرازي: لا يكون العذاب لأنه لم يكن حاصلا في ذلك الوقت

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Al-Qaffāl allows رجس to mean an increase in disbelief through a stain on hearts, comparing it with 9:125; رجس can mean displeasure or spiritual stain, making وقع past tense literal, whereas punishment would use a past for a certain future.
rows.anchor: وقال القفال: يجوز أن يكون الازدياد في الكفر بالرين على القلوب أي لتماديهم على الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dispute concerns a futile argument about invented names with no object worthy of worship; سميتموها means you and your fathers coined the names.
rows.anchor: هذا إنكار منه لمخاصمتهم له فيما لا ينبغي فيه الخصام وهو ذكر ألفاظ ليس تحتها مدلول يستحق العبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols were called Ṣamūd, Ṣadāʾ, and al-Habāʾ; Murthad ibn Saʿd's poem names them and depicts the people as destroyed by drought.
rows.anchor: وهي صمود وصداء والهباء وقد ذكرها مرثد بن سعد في شعره فقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, names stands for the named idols by ellipsis: they were arguing about statues they named as gods and worshipped apart from God.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون الجدال وقع في المسميات وهي الأصنام فيكون أطلق الأسماء وأراد بها المسميات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says they assigned each idol a desired function, such as bringing rain, healing sickness, accompanying travel, or supplying provision.
rows.anchor: قيل: سموا كل صنم باسم على ما اشتهوا وزعموا أن بعضهم يسقيهم المطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God saved Hūd and those who believed through prior mercy and favor; granting them faith became the means of their rescue from the punishment.
rows.anchor: فأنجيناه والذين معه برحمة منا يعني من آمن معه برحمة سابقة لهم من الله وفضل عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cutting the disbelievers' rear is a figure for utterly destroying them by punishment.
rows.anchor: وقطعنا دابر الذين كذبوا بآياتنا كناية عن استئصالهم بالهلاك بالعذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling them those who denied God's signs identifies their denial as the reason for their destruction and implies that Hūd had miracles, though their specifics are not given.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله بآياتنا دليل على أنه كانت لهود معجزات ولكن لم تذكر لنا بتعيينها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وما كانوا مؤمنين may emphasize their denial, or report that God knew they would never believe; a denier might later repent, but those decreed to remain disbelievers never believe.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون إخبارا من الله تعالى أنهم ممن علم الله تعالى أنهم لو بقوا لم يؤمنوا

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī reads the ending as distinguishing the destroyed disbelievers from believers such as Murthad and Hūd's rescued followers: destruction struck only those who denied.
rows.anchor: ليؤذن أن الهلاك خص المكذبين ونجى الله المؤمنين قاله الزمخشري:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author omits exegetical tales about ʿĀd's destruction when they do not connect to Qur'anic wording or are not authentically from the Prophet, treating text-related details in their proper places.
rows.anchor: وذكر المفسرون هنا قصة هلاك عاد وذكروا فيها أشياء لا تعلق لها بلفظ القرآن ولا صحت عن الرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thamūd is the name of the tribe, after its ancestor Thamūd, brother of Jadīs; both were sons of Jāthir, son of Iram, son of Sam, son of Noah.
rows.anchor: ثمود اسم القبيلة سميت باسم أبيهم الأكبر وهو ثمود أخو جديس وهما ابنا جاثر بن إرم بن سام بن نوح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation derives the Thamud name from thamad, meaning scant water.
rows.anchor: وقيل سميت ثمود لقلة ما بها من الثمد وهو الماء القليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thamud homes were in al-Ḥijr between the Ḥijāz and Syria, extending to Wādī al-Qurā.
rows.anchor: وكانت مساكنهم الحجر بين الحجاز والشام وإلى وادي القرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause uses نزل here and أنزل elsewhere; both are eloquent, with equivalent transitivity through gemination or hamza.
rows.anchor: وجاء هنا نزل وفي مكان غيره أنزل وكلاهما فصيح والتعدية بالتضعيف والهمزة سواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to wait is a final threat to await the consequences of idolatry and rejecting the messenger, with certainty that they will occur.
rows.anchor: فانتظروا إني معكم من المنتظرين وهذا غاية في التهديد والوعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed poet uses الثمد in a verse about a neighborhood girl looking toward birds coming to a small pool, supporting the name's association with scant water.
rows.anchor: إلى حمام شراع وارد الثمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thamūd were prosperous Arabs who rebelled, worshipped other than God, and corrupted the land; God sent Salih, of distinguished lineage and standing, who preached until gray-haired, with few followers.
rows.anchor: وكانت ثمود عربا في سعة من العيش فخالفوا أمر الله وعبدوا غيره وأفسدوا فبعث الله لهم صالحا نبيا

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Wahb says Salih was sent when approaching puberty; after his people perished, he and his followers migrated to Mecca, where they remained until death and were buried between Dar al-Nadwa and al-Ḥijr.
rows.anchor: قاله وهب: بعثه الله حين راهق الحلم فلما هلك قومه ارتحل بمن معه إلى مكة

rows.speaker: الشريف النسابة الجواني
rows.claim: The genealogist al-Jawānī gives Salih's lineage as Salih son of Asaf, son of Kāshiḥ, son of Arūm, son of Thamūd, son of Jāthir, son of Iram, son of Sam, son of Noah.
rows.anchor: هكذا نسبه الشريف النسابة الجواني وهو المنتهى إليه في علم النسب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some exegetical genealogies insert ʿUbayd as a father between Salih and Asaf, omit ancestors, and corrupt Jāthir to ʿĀbir; al-Jawānī's genealogy restores the line.
rows.anchor: ووقع في بعض التفاسير بين صالح وآسف زيادة أب وهو عبيد فقالوا صالح بن عبيد بن آسف

rows.speaker: ابن وثاب والأعمش
rows.claim: Ibn Waththāb and al-Aʿmash read ثمود with kasra on dāl and nunation throughout the Qur'an, treating it as the name of the people; the majority leave it uninflected as a tribal name.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن وثاب والأعمش: وإلى ثمود بكسر الدال والتنوين مصروفا في جميع القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Brotherhood here means kinship: Salih and the people descend from the same ancestor, Thamūd son of Jāthir.
rows.anchor: والأخوة هنا في القرابة، لأن نسبه ونسبهم راجع إلى ثمود بن جاثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah, Hūd, and Salih all called their idol-worshipping peoples to worship God alone; these stories reproach and warn the Arabs, including Quraysh, of total destruction like earlier peoples.
rows.anchor: وكل واحد من هؤلاء الأنبياء نوح وهود وصالح تواردوا على الأمر بعبادة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah's story was widely known, and Hūd and Salih were known among Arabs and others; pre-Islamic poets invoked those peoples when describing corrupt groups.
rows.anchor: وكانت قصة نوح مشهورة طبقت الآفاق وقصة هود وصالح مشهورة عند العرب وغيرهم بحيث ذكرها قدماء الشعراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A pre-Islamic poet compares his own people to the corrupt people of earlier times, using عادوا as poetic evidence of that allusion.
rows.anchor: فينا معاشر لن يبغوا لقومهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The she-camel and her calf were familiar to pre-Islamic Arabs, who mentioned the calf in poetry about warriors all killed in battle.
rows.anchor: وهذه الناقة وسقبها مشهور قصتهما عند جاهلية العرب وقد ذكروا السقب في أشعارهم

rows.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري
rows.claim: Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī says he measured the she-camel's chest in Thamūd's land and found it sixty cubits.
rows.anchor: قال أبو موسى الأشعري: أتيت أرض ثمود فذرعت صدر الناقة فوجدته ستين ذراعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attributing her grazing land to God reminds them that the earth and its growth belong to Him, not them; the camel is a gift whose milk requires no labor to feed her.
rows.anchor: لما أضاف الناقة إلى الله أضاف محل رعيها إلى الله إذ الأرض وما أنبت فيها ملكه تعالى

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik cites the report about a stray camel: it carries its own water and shoes, finds water and eats trees until its owner meets it, illustrating the she-camel's self-sufficiency.
rows.anchor: قال مالك: ولها معها سقاؤها وحذاؤها ترد الماء وتأكل الشجر حتى يلقاها ربها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The jussive تأكل answers the command to leave her; Abū Jaʿfar reads it nominative as a circumstantial clause.
rows.anchor: وتأكل جزم على جواب الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The camel and calf grazed and drank, returning to water every other day; on her turn she drained the well, then they milked her until all vessels were filled for drinking and storage.
rows.anchor: كانت الناقة مع ولدها ترعى الشجر وتشرب الماء ترد غبا فإذا كان يومها وضعت رأسها في البئر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ban on even touching her harmfully implies an even stronger ban on slaughtering, hamstringing, or withholding water and pasture; touching and taking are figurative expressions.
rows.anchor: وهذا تنبيه بالأدنى على الأعلى إذا كان قد نهاهم عن مسها بسوء إكراما لآية الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning's painful punishment is what befell them when they hamstrung her and what awaits them in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: والعذاب الأليم هو ما حل بهم إذ عقروها وما أعد لهم في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Salih recalls their succession after ʿĀd and their distinctive settlement with palaces on the plains and houses carved into mountains; like Hūd, he then recalls God's general blessings.
rows.anchor: ذكر صالح قومه بما ذكر به هود قومه فذكر أولا نعما خاصة وهي جعلهم خلفاء بعد الأمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بوأكم means He settled you in the land; أرض here is al-Ḥijr between the Ḥijāz and Syria, while taking palaces from the plains likely means only some plains were built up.
rows.anchor: ومعنى وبوأكم في الأرض أنزلكم بها وأسكنكم إياها والمباءة المنزل في الأرض

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī interprets palaces from the plains as built from soft earth materials such as mudbrick, fired brick, and plaster, as the calf's image was made from gold ornaments.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: من سهولها قصورا أي يبنونها من سهولة الأرض بما يعملون منها الرهض واللبن والآجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ظاهر الاتخاذ means actual construction and takes one object; another analysis makes the construction take two objects, with the prepositional phrase as the second.
rows.anchor: وظاهر الاتخاذ هنا العمل فيتعدى تتخذون إلى مفعول واحد

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads وتنحتون with fatḥa on the ḥāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وتنحتون بفتح الحاء

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī also gives the lengthened reading وتنحاتون, citing a poetic line as a parallel form.
rows.anchor: وزاد الزمخشري: أنه قرأ وتنحاتون بإشباع الفتحة قال كقوله

rows.speaker: ابن مصرف
rows.claim: Ibn Muṣarrif reads the verb with yāʾ and kasra on the ḥāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن مصرف بالياء من أسفل وكسر الحاء

rows.speaker: أبو مالك
rows.claim: Abū Mālik reads with bāʾ in place of the initial tāʾ and fatḥa on the ḥāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو مالك بالباء من أسفل وفتح الحاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reading the verb with yāʾ is a shift in grammatical person.
rows.anchor: ومن نقرأ بالياء فهو التفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بيوتا may be a resultative circumstantial accusative, since mountains were not houses before carving; alternatively, it is a second object under a meaning of taking, or the object of carving with mountains as an object governed by an omitted من.
rows.anchor: وانتصب بيوتا على أنها حال مقدرة إذ لم تكن الجبال وقت النحت بيوتا

rows.speaker: الأعمش
rows.claim: Al-Aʿmash reads تعثوا with kasra on tāʾ, a dialect also heard in أنت تعلم; مفسدين is an emphatic circumstantial expression.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش تعثوا بكسر التاء لقولهم أنت تعلم وهي لغة ومفسدين حال مؤكدة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the plains palaces were for summer and mountain houses for winter.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: القصور لمصيفهم والبيوت في الجبال لمشتاهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says the people carved mountain homes because their long lives outlasted their palaces; Wahb describes repeated rebuilding every century before they turned to mountains.
rows.anchor: وقيل: نحتوا الجبال لطول أعمارهم كانت القصور تخرب قبل موتهم، قال وهب:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads وقال الملأ with a conjunction, while the majority read قال الملأ without one.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر وقال الملأ بواو عطف والجمهور قال بغير واو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the chiefs استكبروا may distinguish them because some chiefs believed, including Jundaʿ ibn ʿAmr, or it may be a condemnatory description; the form may mean seeking grandeur or simply becoming proud.
rows.anchor: والذين استكبروا وصف للملأ إما للتخصيص لأن من أشرافهم من آمن مثل جندع بن عمرو وإما للذم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The weak are the leaders' humiliated common followers; لمن آمن may make believers a subset of them or explain them, depending on whether منهم refers to the weak or to Salih's people.
rows.anchor: والذين استضعفوا أي استضعفهم رؤساء الكفار واستذلوهم وهم العامة وهم أتباع الرسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The chiefs' question about Salih being sent by his Lord is sarcastic and singles him out rather than saying our Lord or your Lord.
rows.anchor: واللام في للذين للتبليغ والجملة المقولة استفهام على جهة الاستهزاء والاستخفاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers wisely affirm faith in Salih's message instead of answering whether he was sent: his extraordinary sign makes prophethood clear, leaving only assent to what he brought.
rows.anchor: إذ أمر رسالته معلوم واضح مسلم لا يدخله ريب لما أتى به من هذا المعجز الخارق العظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The chiefs' wording is semantically the same as the believers' phrase but verbally broader, so they reject the fact the believers treated as settled.
rows.anchor: فالذي آمنتم به هو من حيث المعنى بما أرسل به لكنه من حيث اللفظ أعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The whole community is credited with hamstringing the camel although only some did it, because the act came from concerted agreement; one report says Qudār consulted men, women, and children.
rows.anchor: نسب العقر إلى الجميع وإن كان صادرا عن بعضهم لما كان عقرها عن تمالئ واتفاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reported cause is that the camel displaced livestock between valley slopes according to season, consumed the community's water, and was milked until they wearied of milk and preferred water.
rows.anchor: وسبب عقرها أنها كانت إذا وقع الحر نصبت بظهر الوادي فتهرب منها أنعامهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the same report, Salih foretold that a newborn would bring their destruction; nine men killed their sons, while Salif son of Qudār survived, grew extraordinarily fast, and angered them because he made them regret killing their children.
rows.anchor: وقال لهم صالح يوما إن هذا الشهر يولد فيه مولود يكون هلاككم على يديه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nine plotted to kill Salih and hid for an ambush; the account continues in Sūrat al-Naml.
rows.anchor: فأجمعوا على قتله فكمنوا له في غار ليبيتوه، ويأتي خبر التبييت وما جرى لهم في سورة النمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A pre-Islamic poet calls the rapidly growing Qudār أحمر عاد; commentators correct the tribal name to أحمر ثمود.
rows.anchor: فتنتج لكم غلمان أشأم كلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account blames two women opposed to Salih: ʿUnayza offered Qudār a daughter, while Ṣadūf offered herself to al-Ḥubāb, then to her cousin Muṣdaʿ; Qudār and Muṣdaʿ recruited seven accomplices.
rows.anchor: وروي أن السبب في عقرها أن امرأتين من ثمود من أعداء صالح وهما عنيزة بنت غنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nine lay in wait as the camel left the water: Qudār hid by a rock and Muṣdaʿ by another, and Muṣdaʿ's arrow pierced her leg muscle.
rows.anchor: فرصدوا الناقة حين صدرت عن الماء وكمن قدار في أصل صخرة ومصدع في أصل أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the ambush account, Qudār cut the camel's hamstrings, she fell and cried once, then he stabbed and slaughtered her; the townspeople divided and cooked her meat.
rows.anchor: فشد عليها بالسيف فكشف عرقوبها فخرت ورغت رغاة واحدة فطعن في لبتها ونحرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source mentions another tale about the camel's speed but says God knows whether it is authentic.
rows.anchor: وذكروا لسبقها حكاية الله أعلم بصحتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative cause says Qudār drank wine, could not find water to mix because the camel had consumed it, and resolved to hamstring her with a spear.
rows.anchor: وقيل سبب عقرها أن قدارا شرب الخمر وطلبوا ماء لمزجها فلم يجدوه لشرب الناقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An Arab poet depicts the killer as a reddish youth with a sword who declares the camel slain.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض شعراء العرب وقد ذكر قصة الناقة:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: عتوا عن أمر ربهم means they arrogantly defied God's order, delivered by Salih, to let the camel graze and not harm her; it can also mean their defiance arose from that order.
rows.anchor: أي استكبروا عن امتثال أمر ربهم وهو ما أمر به تعالى على لسان صالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second grammatical reading makes their rebellion proceed from God's command to leave the camel, as in the wording وما فعلته عن أمري.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المعنى صدر عتوهم عن أمر ربهم كأن أمر ربهم بتركها كان هو السبب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their demand for the promised punishment shows they hastened the threat while denying both the warning and Salih's messengership.
rows.anchor: فاستعجلوا ما وعدهم به من ذلك إذ كانوا مكذبين له في الإخبار بذلك الوعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Warsh and al-Aʿmash read يا صالح ائتنا; Abū ʿAmr changes the initial hamza when joining, while the other canonical readers keep it still.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ورش والأعمش يا صالح ائتنا وأبو عمرو إذا أدرج بإبدال همزة فاء ائتنا واو الضمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya cites Abū Ḥātim's report that ʿĪsā and ʿĀṣim read أوتنا with hamza and lengthened ḍamma, likely ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī rather than the canonical ʿĀṣim ibn Abī al-Najūd.
rows.anchor: وفي كتاب ابن عطية قال أبو حاتم: قرأ عيسى وعاصم أوتنا بهمز وإشباع ضم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the calf roared three times; Salih assigned one day to each roar, predicting yellow, red, then black faces and punishment on Sunday, the first appointed day.
rows.anchor: روي أن السقب لما عقروا الناقة رغا ثلاثا فقال صالح لكل رغوة أجل يوم تمتعوا في داركم ثلاثة أيام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nine plotters sought Salih's death, but angels crushed them with stones; their accusation that Salih killed them and attempt to kill him failed when his clan protected him.
rows.anchor: فرام التسعة عاقر والناقة قتله وبيتوه فدمغتهم الملائكة بالحجارة
